## Summary

I reviewed all 10 source files in the `app/` package — a "signed job envelope" service where `routes.submit_job` feeds untrusted request data into `jobs.process_job`.

**Two exploitable findings, both rooted in `app/jobs.py`:**

1. **`insecure-deserialization` (CRITICAL)** — `pickle.loads(decoded)` runs on attacker-controlled bytes from the request body. A crafted `__reduce__` payload executes arbitrary code during deserialization. The HMAC signature (the only auth mechanism) is verified *after* `pickle.loads`, so it offers zero protection against this code path. A safe JSON parser already exists in the codebase (`json_jobs.load_json_job`), confirming the pickle use is gratuitous.

2. **`authentication-bypass` (HIGH)** — The signature is checked *after* the privileged branch `if job.get('role') == 'admin': run_privileged(job)` has already dispatched to `admin_queue.submit`. The `PermissionError` raised by `verify_signature` only fires once the privileged action has already executed, and the `role` field is read from not-yet-authenticated data. An attacker controlling the body can set `role='admin'` with an empty/invalid `X-Signature` and still reach the privileged code path.

**Considered and excluded (no exploitable issue):** `storage.py` uses parameterized SQL (`?` placeholders, no injection); `json_jobs.py` uses safe `json.loads` (Python has no prototype pollution); `schema.py`/`worker.py` validate the action against an allowlist before dispatch; `logging.py` deliberately omits sensitive args; `config.py` uses env vars with safe defaults; `signatures.py` uses `hmac.compare_digest` correctly (but is defeated by ordering in `jobs.py`). No dependency manifest exists, so no `vulnerable-dependency` finding; no CORS/redirect/template/path/SSRF/mass-assignment sinks are present.
